problems: The blind guess (a giraffe or long-necked animal with a small quadruped below) does not match the intended subject. The drawing reads as a long straight stick with a looped top, not as an animal.
The hook is drawn as a loose blue loop that reads more like a rope or a neck than a crook. Its curl does not start clearly at the crown (89341) and turn back toward the herd at the tip (88116).

The separate blue outline at roughly x 205-265, y 280-340, with a small body and legs, is a quadruped-like figure. It is the most animal-like element, which explains the giraffe guess, and it competes with the crook for attention.
A wavy horizontal blue line at roughly x 187-333, y 345-360 sits under the figure. It reads as ground or a stream and adds to the animal-scene impression.

Labels collide with the drawing and with each other. The 'bend of the shaft just below the hook' label runs into the 'tip of the hook' label. The 'grip, middle of the shaft' label crosses the shaft line.
Two labels are truncated in the frame: 'crown of the hook, where the' and 'ferrule, the iron foot of th'.

Positive: the figure is upright, with the ferrule (89642, about 170,470) at the bottom and the hook at the top. The shaft runs from the ferrule through the lower shaft (90185, about 137,417), grip (89931, about 150,312), upper shaft (89678, about 164,247) and bend (89153, about 197,170) to the crown (89341, about 185,107). The tip (88116, about 258,172) sits at the end of the hook. Each key star sits on the part it names.
output.advice: Redraw so the crook reads unambiguously as a shepherd's crook and not as an animal. (1) Keep the straight shaft from ferrule 89642 (~170,470) up through 90185 (~137,417), 89931 (~150,312), 89678 (~164,247) to the bend 89153 (~197,170), but make it a clean, nearly straight line with a slight taper at the bottom. (2) Replace the loose loop with a tight, closed hook. Start it at the crown 89341 (~185,107), arc it clockwise over the top to the right, and curl it back down so the tip 88116 (~258,172) turns inward toward the herd. The inner radius should be small enough that the hook reads as a J-curve, not a neck. (3) Remove the quadruped outline at ~205-265, 280-340, and the wavy ground line at y ~345-360. If a herd is needed, place a few tiny unlabelled dots or small sheep shapes to the right of the shaft at about x 280-340, y 250-350, clearly separate from the crook. (4) Move labels so they do not cross strokes. Put the 'bend' label left of the shaft and the 'tip' label right of the hook. Shorten the 'crown' and 'ferrule' labels so they are not truncated. (5) Keep the gold lines on the shaft and hook path, and make sure the blue silhouette is not a copy of them."]
